comments.author: @Charlies_Little_Corner
comments.text: 5:41 while I'm sympathetic to your view on regulation, it has an important caveat and needs some clarification. The EU consumer care regulation is built around the principle "regulate before something happens" whereas US regulation (see Flint etc.) usually is built around "regulate something after it happens". That's no small difference and would need a deep dive into the philosophy of law (case law vs. written law). The caveat, and this pops up all around AI recently, any technology that may be beneficial to some members of society can in principle also be misused. There is a risk of "weaponized compassion" there, based on the transhumanist assumption that we need not only to overcome the limits of our bodies, but also overcome death itself to have a fulfilled and valuable life. At the very least, AI development invites us to seriously think about these questions.
